note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, schedule, price and lighting answer below comes from the City of Tallahassee's own pickleball page, which lists each outdoor venue with an address, a count line in the City's words and a weekly grid of Open Play, Reserved Play and First-Come First-Play, then defines the three terms and prices the middle one. Three community centre pages (Walker-Ford, Jack L. McLean Jr. and Sue Herndon McCollum) supply building hours and a second copy of an address. Where the City is silent, on surface everywhere, on lighting at six of the seven venues and on parking anywhere, this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
The City of Tallahassee publishes nothing about parking at any of the seven venues on this page. The word does not appear on the pickleball page, and the community centre pages give hours and a phone number without mentioning a lot.

Four of the seven venues are community centres with the courts outside the building. Walker-Ford and McLean are open Monday to Saturday 9:00am to 9:00pm, and the Sue McCollum centre in Lafayette Park Monday to Friday 9:00am to 9:00pm and Saturday from 1:00pm. That clock matters at Lafayette Park, because paddles and balls are "available inside the Sue McCollum Community Center only during regular office hours". The McLean page lists "two comfort stations", the one mention of restrooms at any published venue.
slots.peak_hours:
Tallahassee publishes a weekly timetable for its outdoor courts, and the timetable is the peak hours answer. The rule is stated once: "All Outdoor Courts are First-Come First-Play except during the times noted below". Open Play is free and drop-in. Reserved Play is booked and paid for.

At LeVerne Payne, Open Play runs Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings 8:00am-12:00pm for beginners and advanced beginners, with an intermediate session Saturday 2:00pm-5:00pm. At Tom Brown Park it runs Monday and Wednesday 8:00am-12:00pm and Sunday 8:00am-12:00pm and 5:00pm-8:30pm, with Reserved Play filling the weekday evenings. Winthrop Park has Reserved Play and no Open Play at all. Jake Gaither carries the one clock time hours line in the city, "Outdoor FCFP: 8:00am - 9:00pm Daily, Closed on Sunday".

Inside Open Play the "RACK" sets the order, games go to 11 and win by 2, and drop to 9 points once six players are waiting. Outside any session, first come play carries a 90 minute limit when others are waiting.
slots.surface_condition:
The City names no surface for any pickleball court in Tallahassee. The nearest it comes is a rule at Winthrop Park, whose courts are for "tennis, pickleball and any other sports that will not damage the surface or nets of the courts".

What the City does describe is the hardware. LeVerne Payne has "2 courts with adjustable net straps, 4 courts with portable nets if needed and all have painted lines". McLean's two have adjustable net straps and painted lines, and Lafayette Park's two have net tie-downs. Eight of Tom Brown's twelve sit on tennis courts 1 to 4, and Winthrop's six are multi-purpose as well, so fourteen of the thirty-three outdoor courts are tennis courts taking pickleball.

The one statement about condition is a closure, and it is stale. McLean's line still reads "Due to scheduled resurfacing, both the outdoor tennis and pickleball courts at jack mclean will be unavailable for  use until december 5, 2025."
slots.local_scene:
Thirty-four verified courts across seven City venues, thirty-three of them outdoors and one inside Jake Gaither Community Center. Tom Brown Park's twelve is the largest published set. Tallahassee is the third Florida city on this site after Cape Coral and Tampa, the first in Leon County, and the city that puts Florida over the three-city threshold for a state page.

The City writes more about how play is organised than most. It is the first operator on this site to publish a written open-play rotation rule - the "RACK" sets the order, games go to 11, and to 9 once six players are waiting. LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown publish as free, because the City schedules Open Play there and writes that "all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free". The other five are unpriced first come courts.

Five venues the City lists are not published. The largest is Four Oaks Park, six courts "used for pickleball only" at an address, "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard", that neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts and a free morning
best_for.text: Tom Brown Park has twelve outdoor courts on the City's line: four standalone and eight lined onto tennis courts 1 to 4. It is the largest published set in Tallahassee. Open Play, drop-in and free, runs Monday and Wednesday mornings and Sunday morning and evening. Reserved Play at $3.50 to $5.75 a session fills the weekday evenings and can be booked online. Lighting and surface are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you are new and want a session made for you
best_for.text: LeVerne Payne Community Center schedules "Beginner & Adv. Beginner Open Play" on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings 8:00am-12:00pm and "Intermed. Open Play" on Saturday afternoons, all free, on six courts: two with fixed nets and four painted for portable ones. The City's Wednesday morning clinics run here too. Phone 850-891-3930. Lighting and surface are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to play after dark
best_for.text: Walker-Ford Community Center is the one Tallahassee venue where the City says its courts can be used at night. Its three courts carry the line "night play is available". The word is "night play", not "lighted", and the lighting answer is published on that phrase. The courts are first come, first play at all hours, with a 90 minute limit when others are waiting, and no price is stated.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Tallahassee have?
faqs.a: Thirty-four across seven City venues: 33 outdoor and one indoor. Tom Brown Park has twelve, LeVerne Payne and Winthrop six each, Walker-Ford and Jake Gaither three each, and McLean and Lafayette Park two each.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Tallahassee?
faqs.a: During Open Play, yes, and the City says so: "all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free". Open Play is scheduled at LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown. Reserved Play costs $5.75 singles and $4.25 doubles, with senior rates of $4.75 and $3.50 from age 62. The other five venues carry no stated price.
